notes: Eclipse Loop 1.5.4 Drum levels in the step sequencer, and session recording that stops lying about permissions. This release also carries the 1.5.3 fix below, which was built and signed but never published — if you are on 1.5.2, this is the first build that delivers it. Changed - STUTTER is a lighter touch. Instead of filling whole bars, it now rebuilds a handful of single beats as soft, edge-faded rolls, leaving most of the loop alone. The number of spots scales with length — roughly one per four bars, between three and eight — so it reads the same on a 4-bar loop as on a 36-bar one. Fixed - Loud one-shots played almost silently in the sequencer. With RELEASE turned up, the release fade was measured against the release time rather than the sample, so for anything shorter than that time the fade began before the hit started — a kick or snare played at roughly a tenth of its level and faded out. Loud drum samples read as "barely audible at full volume." The body of a sample now always plays at full level and only a genuine tail fades. (Carried over from 1.5.3.) - ON AIR session recording reported "permission is off" when it was on. macOS ties the Screen Recording permission to the exact app build, so installing an update silently revokes it while System Settings still shows the switch enabled. The old message sent you to that switch, which already looked correct, and there was no way to tell the difference from a real denial. The message now explains what actually happened and tells you to toggle Eclipse Loop off and back on, which is what re-authorises the new build. Note for anyone updating If session recording stops working after this update, that is the macOS behaviour described above, not a fault in the app: turn Eclipse Loop off and then back on in System Settings ▸ Privacy & Security ▸ Screen & System Audio Recording, then quit and reopen Eclipse Loop. Expect to do this after each update.
